sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 1:1
items.html: Everything in the worlds that exists as “existence from existence,” which is everything but the substance of the vessels (see Items 2 and 24).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 2:1
items.html: The will to receive in the emanated being is called “vessel,” and the abundance that he receives is called “light.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 3:1
items.html: A light that makes no distinction of degrees.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 4:1
items.html: A light that contains within it the vessels, to the point that the light and the vessel are indistinguishable.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 5:1
items.html: A light that is extended to the emanated being in the first expansion, which is all the vitality and self of the emanated being.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 6:1
items.html: A light that clothes the light of Hochma, and is extended to the emanated being with the first intensification.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 7:1
items.html: It is light of Hassadim before it is clothed on the light of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 8:1
items.html: That which stems from its previous phase, see Item 20.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 9:1
items.html: See item 39.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 10:1
items.html: The upper light that expands from His self is one and as simple as His self. As it is in Ein Sof, so it is even in the world of Assiya, without any change and addition of form at all; this is why it is called “One.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 11:1
items.html: The name Creator relates solely to the innovation, meaning the making of “existence from absence,” which is the substance of the vessels, defined as the “will to receive” in every essence. It was necessarily absent in His self prior to creation.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 12:1
items.html: It is equivalence of form that brings the spirituals closer and attaches them to one another, while disparity of form moves them away from one another.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 13:1
items.html: When there is no distinction whatsoever among the four phases of the will to receive, it is said that they are in equivalence.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 14:1
items.html: Light that stems from the emanator to the emanated being is called “expansion of light.” But in fact, the upper light is not affected by that. It is like lighting one candle from another, where the first is not lessened. It is called so because of the reception of the emanated being.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 15:1
items.html: Phase one in the will to receive is regarded as more refined than the three phases that follow it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 16:1
items.html: It is a certain sum of phases that cascade from one another and are mingled in one another by an order of cause and consequence, such as days, months, and years.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 17:1
items.html: Phase four in the desire, which does not receive the upper light inside it because of the restriction, is regarded as the root of darkness.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 18:1
items.html: It is the light of the very vitality of the emanated being (see item 5).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 19:1
items.html: Phase four in the desire, which was emptied of light, is regarded as darkness compared to the light. With respect to the vessel, she is regarded as a space, since phase four, in its self, was not deprived from the emanated being in itself by the restriction, but is there in it as an empty space without light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 20:1
items.html: When speaking of a relationship of cause and consequence of the emanated beings, we express the cause by the word “before” and the consequence of that consequence by the word “after.” (see item 16).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 21:1
items.html: Unique indicates the upper light that shines and rules over all the many degrees, which are different from each other, to the point of inverting them and equalizing them with His unique form. “Unified” indicates the end of that rule, meaning after He had already equalized and returned their form to the state of “unique,” as He is (see item 14).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 22:1
items.html: Two different phases that have equalized their form with one another unite into one phase (see item 12).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 23:1
items.html: Sometimes, an inferior degree ascends to an equal level with the one above it, when the upper one needs it for its own completion. In that state, the lower one is regarded as “left” and the upper one as “right.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 24:1
items.html: The title “Maker” relates to the pouring of the light into the worlds, which includes everything but the substance of the vessels (see above items 11 and 1).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 25:1
items.html: The will to receive in the emanated being is his vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 26:1
items.html: Equivalence of form of the lower one with the upper one is an “ascent upward.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 27:1
items.html: Any cause is regarded as the emanator of the degree that results from it. The title “Emanator” contains both the extension of the light, and the vessel that receives the light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 28:1
items.html: The will to receive that was imprinted in the souls is what separates them and “carves” them off from the upper light. That is because disparity of form separates in spirituality (see item 12). The matter of the origin of the soul refers to the transition between the world of Atzilut and the world of Beria, which will be explained in its place.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 29:1
items.html: The one of a lesser merit than the other is regarded as being “below” the other.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 30:1
items.html: See above the word “Unique.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 31:1
items.html: It is the will to receive that is necessarily there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 32:1
items.html: Meaning from phase one to phase four. Phase four that was left without light, is regarded as being “below” all the degrees. The weaker the will to receive, the higher one is considered to be. Therefore, phase one is regarded as the “highest” of all.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 33:1
items.html: Where there is no deficiency whatsoever, and where an addition to the wholeness there is inconceivable.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 34:1
items.html: The more important is regarded as “above,” and the worse as “below.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 35:1
items.html: The will to receive in the emanated being is the “place” for all the abundance and the light in it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 36:1
items.html: It is a degree that consists of all four phases of the desire.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 37:1
items.html: It is a degree with only the first three phases of the desire.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 38:1
items.html: If the disparity of form of the degree from the root is not so apparent as to separate it from the root, it is regarded as “touching” the root. The same applies between each two adjacent degrees.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 39:1
items.html: Phase four in Ein Sof is called so after its unification with the light of Ein Sof.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 40:1
items.html: The Sof and the Sium [also “end/conclusion”] of every emanated being is done by the detaining force in phase four, where the upper light stops shining because she does not receive it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 41:1
items.html: If there is no discernment of above and below among the four phases of the will to receive, it is regarded as a circle (like an image of a corporeal circle, where there is no discernment of up or down). Because of that, the four phases are regarded as four concentric circles one inside the other, where it is impossible to distinguish up from down in them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 42:1
items.html: It is the more important.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 43:1
items.html: Two degrees without any equivalence of form on any side are regarded as completely separate from one another.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 44:1
items.html: This is a place that is prepared to receive corrections and wholeness.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 45:1
items.html: Where there are no discernments of degrees and sides.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 46:1
items.html: One who conquers one’s desire. In other words, one who restrains oneself and does not receive despite one’s great desire to receive, is regarded as restricting oneself.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 47:1
items.html: Indicates a discernment of up and down that was not there before. It also indicates that its illumination is much weaker than before.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 48:1
items.html: The closer one’s form is to another, the closer they are considered to be.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 49:1
items.html: That part in the emanated being that is the most equal to the root is called “Rosh.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 50:1
items.html: Light of Hassadim is called “Ruach.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 51:1
items.html: See item 45.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 52:1
items.html: The Holy Names are explanations of how the lights that they imply are attained. The name of the degree designates the ways of attainment in that degree.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 53:1
items.html: One who receives inside is regarded as the light being measured and limited in the vessel. Conversely, one who receives outside is not regarded as placing any limit on the light that one receives.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Terminology 54:1
items.html: Any new form is regarded as spiritual movement, for it is distinguished from the previous form and acquires a name of its own. It is like a part that is separated from a corporeal object that moves and exits its earlier place.
